title: Streaming reconnect orchestration and token-fragmentation remediation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Post-incident follow-up for a production streaming outage observed on 2026-03-09 where clients experienced abrupt disconnects, partial token delivery, and repeated duplicate reconnect attempts. This ticket coordinates root-cause validation, short-term mitigations, and longer-term runtime changes to make streaming reconnects and partial-token recovery deterministic and cost-stable for customers. Scope includes server-side reconnection orchestration, token-fragment ordering, backpressure handshake improvements, and telemetry to prove behavior improvements across Hosted and Dedicated deployments. Does not include UI/console changes (tracked separately).
root_cause_summary: During a capacity spike and aggressive batching change, workers emitted partially flushed token fragments while downstream connection tear-down logic raced with buffered-appends. The reconnection path lacked a strict resume-protocol (sequence IDs + fragment offsets), so clients either replayed from the last confirmed byte and received duplicates or re-requested and triggered timeouts. Backpressure thresholds tightened under the new batching heuristic causing TCP-level resets that surfaced as streaming disconnects in the API. Combination of: (1) missing idempotent resume protocol for token fragments, (2) batch flush timing regression, and (3) aggressive backpressure threshold changes.

decisions: Introduce a standardized resume token protocol: each streaming chunk will carry a stream_seq (monotonic per-request) and byte_offset to allow exact replay and de-dup checks.
Revert aggressive batching heuristic while we invest in deterministic flush guarantees and per-request backpressure quotas.
Implement server-side reconnection orchestration that coordinates resume attempts and limits duplicate replay windows (max 3 attempts within 30s by default).
Add canary gating for any batching/kernel selection changes with controlled traffic bands and automatic rollback on error rate increase > 10% within 10 minutes.

rollout_plan: Phase 0 (short-term) - conservative rollback applied globally (runtime-1.18): already completed for emergency stabilization
Phase 1 (canary) - enable resume protocol and reconnect orchestrator for 2% of traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with enhanced tracing
Phase 2 (validation) - run 48h canary with scripted reconnect/fuzz tests and monitor duplication/resume metrics
Phase 3 (gradual) - expand to 25% then 100% conditional on no >5% regression in latency SLO or any increase in duplicate token events
Phase 4 - enable for Dedicated and Private customers with opt-in config and compatibility docs
testing_plan: Unit tests for stream_seq/byte_offset encoding/decoding and idempotency checks
Integration test injecting partial flushes and connection resets with assertion on final token sequence matching expected output
Chaos test in staging that saturates worker memory and simulates delayed KV cache writes to exercise backpressure path
Performance regression test to ensure resume metadata adds <1% token throughput overhead in p95 latency
